scope: THREE DISTINCT LENGTHS in arithmetic progression: 55, 76, 97 - a step of exactly 21 bits

the_arithmetic.baseline: 55 = 22 non-value bits + 33 value bits (the gate=1 form of codec -97)
the_arithmetic.step: 76 = 55 + 21, and 97 = 76 + 21, so each extra unit costs exactly 21 bits
the_arithmetic.implication: the value's bits are being consumed BEYOND the 33-bit field, in units of 21 bits, one or two units depending on the value

what_a_21_bit_unit_could_be: a further delta record: 1 bit continuation + 5 bits V + distance + a small value would land near 21
so the value's remaining bits are most likely being read as a NEW field header, producing one or two extra decoded fields
that also explains why value 6 raises a stream error: after two extra units the decoder runs past the terminator
why_the_high_values_are_clean: 255, 256, 512, 1024, 2048 and 4096 all cost exactly 55, so for those the decoder consumed the 33-bit field and stopped
the difference must be in how the low bits of the value look to the decoder AFTER the field - a value whose trailing bits happen to look like a valid header continues, others do not
next: read what 0x66EC30 does with the 8-bit form (push 8) - it is the N-bit reader used by both the 8-bit branch and elsewhere, and its exact bit order matters
then construct a body whose value bits are chosen so the decoder stops exactly at the intended boundary, i.e. pick the value that keeps the parse at 55
